question: Starting July 1, 2026, what is the total (aggregate) Direct Unsubsidized Loan limit for a professional student (e.g., law or medical school) who does not qualify for the interim exception?
answer:
A professional student who doesn't qualify for the interim exception has a $200,000 aggregate limit on unsubsidized loans, reduced by any amount borrowed as a graduate student. [3][4] That limit does not include loans received for undergraduate study. [4] A student who weren't previously in a graduate program can receive up to the full $200,000. [4]

Separately, this student is also subject to the new $257,500 lifetime maximum, which includes undergraduate loans. [3][4] Grad PLUS loans are no longer available to professional students who don't qualify for the exception. [3][4]

As of the June 24, 2026 court stay (page last updated Aug. 24, 2026), some programs previously classed as professional are not treated as professional, and some others now are. Check with your school to see how your program is classified. [3][4]

studyNotes.focus: The question asks for the aggregate Direct Unsubsidized Loan limit for a professional student starting July 1, 2026 who is not eligible for the interim exception.

keyPoints.text: The new professional student aggregate Unsubsidized Loan limit for those ineligible for the interim exception is $200,000 minus any amount received as a graduate student.
Students who are not eligible for the interim exception face the new annual professional Unsubsidized Loan limit of $50,000, versus $20,500 under pre-OBBBA rules.
Students who qualify for the interim exception keep the legacy aggregate limit of $138,500 through the 2028–29 award year or until they lose eligibility, whichever is earlier.
Loan limits do not start over on July 1, 2026; prior Title IV loans count toward the new aggregate for borrowers not enrolled as of June 30, 2026.
